title: Concepts of average rate, speed, constant speed and average speed
summary: Interpret rates as comparisons of quantities, calculate average speed from total distance and total elapsed time, and distinguish constant speed from an average.
objectives: State a rate with both quantities and a meaningful compound unit.
Calculate average rate or average speed using the relevant totals.
Explain why average speed is generally not the arithmetic mean of stage speeds.

blocks.text: A rate describes how one quantity changes relative to another. Write the comparison as
and keep both units, such as litres per minute or kilometres per hour. Speed is the rate at which distance changes with time.
For a whole journey, add every distance and use the total elapsed time, including a stop when the question says to include it. Then calculate
. Constant speed stays unchanged; average speed summarises a journey that may contain several different speeds.

An object moves at constant speed when it covers equal distances in equal times, so its speed never changes. Average speed describes a whole journey with one number, even when the speed changes. A car that travels 120 km in 2 hours has an average speed of 60 km/h, but it need not have travelled at a constant 60 km/h: it may have gone faster on an open road and stopped at traffic lights.

Common errors: averaging the stage speeds instead of dividing total distance by total time; leaving out a stop that the question says to include; and adding times written in different units, such as hours and minutes, without converting them first.

sections.title: Worked example: average production rate

prompt.text: A machine produces 840 components in 12 minutes. Find its average production rate.

content.text: Divide the total output by the total time.

sections.verification_note: At 70 components per minute, 12 minutes produces 70 × 12 = 840 components.

sections.title: Worked example: average speed including a stop

prompt.text: A cyclist travels 30 km in 2 hours, rests for 20 minutes, and then travels another 18 km in 40 minutes. Find the average speed for the entire period.

content.text: Convert the minutes to hours and add all the elapsed times, including the rest.
Divide the total distance by the total elapsed time.

sections.verification_note: 16 km/h × 3 h = 48 km. Without the rest, the time would be 2⅔ h and the average 18 km/h, so including the stop lowers the average, as it should.

prompt.text: A car travels 150 km in 2.5 hours. Find its average speed.

feedback.text: Divide 150 km by 2.5 h. The average speed is 60 km/h.

blocks.text: Name both quantities, align their units, use the relevant totals, divide amount by time, and state the compound unit. For an average speed, do not average the listed speeds unless their time intervals are equal.
